title: Lower-interface-head to shared-phreatic h-link equivalence and nonequivalence

ownership_cases.name: CONSISTENT_TOTAL_STORAGE
ownership_cases.interpretation: The two numerical storage shares sum to the one target h-link storage.

ownership_cases.name: DUPLICATE_COEXTENSIVE_STORAGE
ownership_cases.interpretation: The two states can collapse to nearly equal heads while the common-head response remains wrong because one physical storage volume is counted twice.

gates: For the consistent case, |H_phreatic_like-H_interface| decreases monotonically with C.
For the consistent case, the C=1000/day live solution approaches the 8.05 m h-link target within 1e-5 m.
At finite C the two heads remain distinct, so the lower-interface model is not yet a one-state h-link.
For duplicate coextensive storage at C=1000/day, both heads approach 8.025 m within 1e-5 m and remain at least 0.02 m away from the 8.05 m target.
Both ownership cases close their own numerical two-reservoir bookkeeping.
The duplicate case fails the one-volume geometric h-link storage law even though the two heads nearly coincide.
equivalence_conditions: H_interface and H_phreatic must collapse to the same physical head state.
Vertical resistance/lag between the two state locations must be negligible on the coupling window.
The sum of subsystem-owned storage responses must equal the one physical h-link storage response with no overlap or gap.
SWAP internal memory may remain distinct but must be continued consistently.
forbidden: do not infer current F-GC mode 5 is equivalent to SWBOTB=1
do not use head equality alone as proof of h-link equivalence
do not apply coextensive duplicate-storage conclusions to MAP11 noncoextensive qualification fixtures
